newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine unionist wants new strike on healthcare.
newsitem.headline: Argentine unionist wants new strike on healthcare.

text.p: An Argentine union leader said on Tuesday that he would propose another general strike, this time for 48 hours, if President Carlos Menem deregulates union-controlled social healthcare plans by decree.

Hugo Moyano of the MTA, a hardline faction of the main CGT labor federation, told reporters he wanted a two-day walkout "at the end of October or the beginning of November" to follow last week's 36-hour strike and a 24-hour stoppage in August.
The CGT's second-in-command Juan Palacios, asked about the MTA strike threat, said: "This will be discussed by the labor movement, that is to say, by the CGT."

Unions, already angry at the Peronist government's fiscal austerity program and proposals for more flexible new labor laws, were further angered Tuesday by Menem's promise to use his power of decree to deregulate healthcare.

Argentina has over 300 union-controlled health plans financed by mandatory contributions. In the face of fierce union opposition the government has been trying to eliminate compulsory affiliation with union "obras sociales" since 1993.

"From next year we will be able to choose freely the most efficient and low cost option for our healthcare," Menem told local radio Tuesday. "In this way, among the almost 309 health plans which move about $2.5 billion, affiliates will be able to move according to their own needs and convenience."
But Moyano was skeptical of the benefits to workers.
"If they deregulate the healthcare schemes, and private firms start competing, before long healthcare for workers won't even amount to so much as an aspirin," he said.

The CGT's Palacios agreed deregulation would "hurt workers most of all, because they won't be able to afford expensive private health schemes. I believe it is the government's aim to privatize and commercialize health; this is unacceptable."
